entities.name: The Holy District
entities.summary: The portion of the land set apart for the LORD in the millennial allotment (Ezek 45:1; 48:8-20) - under the project's framing (ADR 0012) a literal future district in restored Israel, 25,000 cubits long and 20,000 broad (ESV; the Hebrew reads 10,000), holding the priests' and Levites' portions with the sanctuary in its midst; together with the city strip it squares to 25,000 (Ezek 48:20).

entities.name: The New Jerusalem
entities.summary: The eternal city of God, descending out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.

entities.name: The Twelve Gates
entities.summary: The twelve gates of the New Jerusalem, each a single pearl, inscribed with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel.

descriptors.statement: The New Jerusalem comes down out of heaven from God.
The city's length, breadth, and height are equal â€” measured as twelve thousand stadia on each side.
The twelve gates of the city are twelve pearls, each gate being made of a single pearl.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The preciousness, purity, and singular costliness of access to God's eternal city â€” pearls in the ancient world were among the most valued materials and, unlike gold, are organic and singular rather than fabricated.

descriptors.statement: The names of the twelve tribes of the sons of Israel are inscribed on the twelve gates.

relations.notes: Twelve gates are part of the city walls (Rev 21:12).
